gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each under-$300 unit costs per kWh over its rated cycle life (BLUETTI Elite 30 mini about $0.11, EcoFlow RIVER 2 Max 500 about $0.19, BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 about $0.34), or its Wh per lb.
standout_why: Compared against Nineteen Lab (the cited page), Portable Power Rank, Powerstation Picks and WhichWatts. Nineteen Lab prints no prices; its only derived figures are runtimes at rated Wh x 0.85, and it quotes the Elite 30 V2's 4.5 W standby without applying it. Portable Power Rank has prices and weights but derives only 85% runtimes (e.g. 24.5 h for a 10 W fan on the Elite 30 V2). Powerstation Picks has no prices and one runtime sentence. WhichWatts gives cost per Wh for two EcoFlow units only ($0.49 and $0.60, page dated Nov 8), so cost per Wh is partly covered. None gives Wh per lb, cost per kWh over rated cycles, wall refill rate, or a small-load runtime that counts standby draw.
decides: It does not overturn ChatGPT's pick, because I could not open a seller page for the Segway Lumina 500 or Pecron E500LFP. On ChatGPT's own card prices (unverified) they would be about $0.39 and $0.47 per rated Wh, below every unit I could read. Among pages I opened, the RIVER 2 Max 500 is lowest per Wh ($0.58) but EcoFlow's store shows it sold out / pre-order. The Elite 30 mini is the lowest in-stock unit I read per Wh ($0.66 through our link), the lightest per Wh (39.5 Wh/lb) and the lowest per kWh over rated cycles, but its 300 W outlet sits below this page's 600 W breakpoint. The Elite 30 V2 costs about $1.01 per Wh, so it wins only on output (600 W, 140 W USB-C) and charging, not on energy per dollar; its gray colors ship Dec 28 or early January, more than four weeks out.
